note: THE SOURCE for the company's site. Every fact the site states about the company is said here, once. What it states about the product - the version, the commands it names - is the engine's, read from the release requirements-engine.txt pins, and never typed here. A null is a fact not decided yet: the page leaves out what depends on it. The demo and the questions beside it are an illustration - a made-up company's plan and the assets that state it - and the page says so; `{name}` in a line is a value the generator fills from beside it, so no number is said twice. The case study's counts are not here at all: the pendulum counts them itself, facts/pendulum.json is the copy, and each stat names the count it shows by `of`.

hero.headline: Your company,
hero.lede: Your code has one source of truth, and a pipeline that tests every change before it ships. Everything else your company says is a copy of a copy, and every copy drifts.

code.title: Your code
code.caption: Every change branches off, is tested, and merges back. There is one main, and it is the truth.

drift.title: Everything else
drift.caption: Every copy forks, then forks again, and nothing ever merges back. Each version drifts on its own, for good.
drift.sting: That is how a customer ends up quoting you last year’s price.

compiled.title: With Wherefore
compiled.caption: Everything else gets what code already has. Change a fact once: your feature pages, docs, deck and demo video follow it, and nothing ships that still says the old thing.

pains.heading: Sound familiar?

items.pain: Every team has a different picture of what is current.
items.detail: Sales sells last quarter’s plan, support answers from last year’s article, and the truth lives in someone’s head.

items.pain: A feature ships, and the world never hears about it.
items.detail: It is built, tested and released. The site, the docs, the deck and the help centre still describe the product before it.

items.pain: Nobody can say which version is true.
items.detail: Search finds six copies of the same claim. None of them says which one was decided, or why.

pains.answer: Wherefore makes the source the one current picture. Every asset is built from it, and a check can require each new feature to reach the site, the docs and the deck before the change lands.

why.heading: Why “Wherefore”
why.juliet: Juliet wasn’t asking where Romeo was. She was asking why he had to be who he was.
why.rule: In a Wherefore repository every file has to answer her: generated from a source, written by a person for a stated reason, or captured and stamped with what it was made from. A file that cannot answer stops the change.

asks.name: {after}
asks.because: Customers kept calling them projects; only we said workspace. The reason was written down with the change, so it ships with it.

asks.name: demo video
asks.because: My script and captions are built from the same names as the app, so I never point at a button the product no longer has.

asks.name: slide 4

asks.name: orange

asks.name: “SOC 2 certified”
asks.because: I am not allowed yet. Until the audit is signed, the most any page may say is “SOC 2 in progress”, and the check refuses the rest.

does.heading: Everything it does.
does.intro: Built from the release this page pins. Every feature it ships is here, in our words: a release that adds one this page does not describe stops the build until it does.

words.scan: Point it at your site or docs: it finds every value you state more than one way, and where the copies disagree.
words.start: One command starts a repository; the skill walks your agent through the first fact.
words.gate: On every push, every file is generated, written for a reason, or captured - or the change stops, and says why.
words.build: Every asset rebuilt from the source, the same way every time, so you see exactly what a change moves.
words.proofs: No check is trusted until it has failed: each proof plants the fault its check exists to catch.
words.retired: Retire a value once - an old price, name or limit - and nothing a person reads may say it again.
words.reach: Each fact is moved, one at a time, and everything that states it must move too.
words.claims: A claim like "SOC 2 certified" may be said only as its rule allows.
words.upstream: Copied something you can't pin, like a partner's spec sheet? The deploy fails the day its source changes.
words.hook: A push that would ship a stale document stops before it leaves your machine.
words.skill: Claude Code or Codex learns the rules from a skill that ships with each release.

case.name: Chaotic Pendulums
case.heading: A hardware company, compiled from one spec file.

model.title: The MK3 pendulum in 3D: drag to turn it, or grab an arm and swing it

case.text: Chaotic Pendulums is a small hardware company, started to test this idea on something with more surface area than software: a desk-sized double pendulum with milled parts, a bronze blade, bearings and a clamp. Wherefore was built alongside it, one rule at a time. If one source can hold machined parts, physics, suppliers and a storefront, it can hold your app, website and docs.
made: Part drawings a machine shop quotes and inspects against, each with its cut file and its solid model
Print-ready 3D files for a prototype, laid out plate by plate
A bill of materials, and a quote bundle a shop’s online tool takes in one drag
The engineering hand-over, frozen at every release so a shop can always find the pack it quoted
The brand: the mark, the hero and the renders, drawn from the object’s own dimensions
The website, and the 3D pendulum that swings on it
held: Load simulations, worked from the real parts’ masses, prove every mount setup holds the pendulum at a torque a hand can give.
Worst-case tolerance stacks prove every screw clamps and never bottoms, at every extreme of every band.
A sweep proves the blade turns a full circle and touches nothing.
The swing on the website is integrated from the physics of the object as it is today, and a check holds every mass and length to the parts.
Move any dimension, and a probe requires every file a supplier receives to move with it, or the change is refused.
